questions.question: An object floats on a liquid if the density of the object is:

options.text: greater than the density of the liquid
equal to the density of the liquid
exactly twice the density of the liquid
less than the density of the liquid

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**less than the density of the liquid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An object will float on a liquid if its density is **less than the density of the liquid**.
 
• This is due to the principle of **buoyancy**, where the upward buoyant force exerted by the liquid balances the weight of the object.
 
• If the density of the object is higher than the liquid, it will sink because the weight of the object is greater than the buoyant force.
 
• Objects with density equal to the liquid's density will remain suspended at any depth within the liquid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buoyancy**

 
 
• Buoyancy is the force exerted by a fluid that opposes the weight of an immersed object.
 
• The magnitude of the buoyant force is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
 
 
• **Archimedes' Principle**
 
 
• It states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
• This principle helps in determining whether an object will float or sink in a fluid.
 
 
 
• **Density**
 
 
• Density is defined as mass per unit volume and is usually expressed in kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m³).
 
• It is a key factor in determining whether an object will float or sink in a fluid.
 
 
 
• **Specific Gravity**
 
 
• Specific gravity is the ratio of the density of a substance to the density of a reference substance (typically water).
 
• If the specific gravity of an object is less than 1, it will float in water.

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 12 cm is melted and recast into 27 identical spheres. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the total surface area of 6 smaller spheres so formed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the original sphere = 12 cm

The large sphere is melted and recast into 27 identical smaller spheres.

**Formula used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr²

**Step 1: Find the radius of the smaller spheres**

Let the radius of each smaller sphere be r.

Volume of the original sphere = Volume of 27 smaller spheres

⇒ (4/3)π(12)³ = 27 × (4/3)πr³

Cancel out common terms:

⇒ 12³ = 27 × r³

⇒ 1728 = 27 × r³

⇒ r³ = 1728 / 27

⇒ r³ = 64

⇒ r = 4 cm

**Step 2: Calculate the surface area**

Surface area of the original sphere = 4π(12)² = 4π(144) = 576π cm²

Surface area of one smaller sphere = 4π(4)² = 4π(16) = 64π cm²

Total surface area of 6 smaller spheres = 6 × 64π = 384π cm²

**Step 3: Find the ratio of surface areas**

Ratio = Surface area of original sphere / Surface area of 6 smaller spheres

⇒ Ratio = 576π / 384π

⇒ Ratio = 576 / 384 = 3 / 2

**∴ The ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the total surface area of 6 smaller spheres is 3:2.**

questions.question: When the liquid is spun rapidly, the denser particles remain to the bottom and the lighter particles stay at the top. This principle is used in -
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Centrifugation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When the liquid is spun rapidly, the denser particles remain to the bottom and the lighter particles stay at the top. This principle is used in **centrifugation.**
 
• **Centrifugation:**
 
 
• It is the process that uses centrifugal force for the separation of two liquids in a mixture.
 
• In this process, the denser component of the mixture migrates away from the axis and the lighter component migrates toward the axis.
 
• It is a technique based on the principle of sedimentation.
 
• It is based on different factors like the density, shape, size, and viscosity of the particles of a mixture or solution.
 
• Examples: extraction of fat from milk, separation of butter from milk. spin-drying of water etc.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9403118ffb7a29a51e0c53a662009d9169b5375a3d044abc178eb6fe2b50b84b.png] ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** washing machine **works on the principle of centrifugation.

 
 
• It is used to squeeze out water from wet clothes.
 
 
 
• The **separation of butter from milk** is separated by the Centrifugation technique.
 
 
• The principle is that the denser particles are forced to the bottom and the lighter particles stay at the top when spun rapidly.
 
 
 
• Centrifugation is also used in **diagnostic laboratories for blood and urine tests.**
 
• **Filtration:**
 
 
• **Filtration** is the process of the solid unwanted particles from a given liquid or gaseous mixture through the pores of a membrane called a filter.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**:
 
 
• Evaporation is a technique that is used in separating a mixture usually a solution of a solvent and a soluble solid.
 
• In this method, the solution is heated until the organic solvent evaporates where it turns into a gas and mostly leaves behind a solid residue.
 
 
 
• **Fractional distillation:**
 
 
• The method of distillation is **used to separate the liquids having sufficient differences in their boiling points.**
 
• Liquids having different boiling points vaporise
 
• at different temperatures, the vapours are cooled and the liquids so formed are collected separately. 
 
• If the difference in boiling points of two liquids is not much, simple distillation cannot be used to separate them because the vapours of such liquids are formed
 
• within the same temperature range and are condensed simultaneously.
 
• To separate a mixture of two or more miscible liquids for which the difference in **boiling points is less than 25ºC,** a fractional distillation process is used.
 
• For example, for the separation of different gases from the air, different factions from petroleum products etc.
 
• Vapours of the liquid with a higher boiling point condense before the vapours of the liquid with a lower boiling point. By the time the vapours reach the top of the fractionating column, they are rich in the more volatile component.
 
• A fractionating column provides many surfaces for heat exchange between the ascending vapours and the descending condensed liquid.
 
• One of the technological applications of fractional distillation is to separate different fractions of crude oil in the **petroleum industry.**

questions.question: Surekha spends 24% of her monthly income on groceries. 16% of it on rent and 55% of the remaining on children's education and others. If she saves ₹5,940 in a month, then how much (in ₹) does she spend on rent?

Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: Metals are usually hard.

Statement 2: All metals are soluble in water.

Statement 3: Some metals can lose their shine due to oxidation.

options.text: Statements 1 and 3 are true; 2 is false.
Statements 1 and 2 are true; 3 is false.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Statements 1 and 3 are true; 2 is false.**__

__**Explanation:-**__

__
 
• **Hardness of Metals (Statement 1):** Metals are known for their hardness, which is a measure of how resistant they are to deformation or indentation. This property makes metals suitable for various applications that require durability and strength, such as construction materials, tools, and machinery. However, it's important to note that there is variability among metals; some are harder than others. For instance, tungsten is one of the hardest metals, while sodium and potassium are soft enough to be cut with a knife. Still, the generalization that metals are usually hard holds true for the vast majority.
 
• **Solubility of Metals in Water (Statement 2)**: The assertion that all metals are soluble in water is incorrect. Most metals do not dissolve in water under normal conditions. Some metals, such as sodium and potassium, react vigorously with water, but this is a chemical reaction producing hydroxides and hydrogen gas rather than a process of dissolving. Metals like gold, silver, and platinum are virtually nonreactive with water. Therefore, the statement that all metals are soluble in water is false.
 
• **Oxidation of Metals (Statement 3):** Many metals can lose their shine due to oxidation, which is a chemical reaction with oxygen. This process often results in the formation of oxides on the metal surface, which can appear as tarnish or rust, especially noticeable on metals like iron, silver, and copper. This loss of shine due to oxidation is a common phenomenon and is the reason behind various preventive measures, including the application of protective coatings and the use of alloys designed to resist corrosion.

**Conclusion:-**__

So, __ Statements 1 and 3 are true; 2 is false.__

questions.question: A fine beam of light becomes visible when it enters a smoke filled room due to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**scattering of light**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Scattering of light occurs when light interacts with particles such as **smoke, dust, or water droplets**, causing it to deviate from its original path.
 
• In a smoke-filled room, tiny particles in the smoke scatter the light, making the beam visible to the human eye.
 
• Scattering is responsible for the visibility of phenomena like the beam of light from projectors or headlights in foggy conditions.
 
• This process is governed by the **principles of Rayleigh or Mie scattering**, depending on the size of the particles involved.
 
• Scattering of light is also the reason why the sky appears blue during the day and red/orange during sunrise and sunset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflection of Light:**

 
 
• Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface such as a mirror or water.
 
• It does not cause the beam to become visible in smoke-filled environments.
 
 
 
• **Refraction of Light:**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another, such as air to water.
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the visibility of light beams in smoke.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion of Light:**
 
 
• Dispersion is the splitting of light into its constituent colors (e.g., a rainbow).
 
• This does not contribute to the visibility of light in a smoke-filled room.
 
 
 
• **Rayleigh Scattering:**
 
 
• Occurs when particles are much smaller than the wavelength of light.
 
• Responsible for the blue color of the sky during the day.
 
 
 
• **Mie Scattering:**
 
 
• Occurs when particles are comparable in size to the wavelength of light.
 
• Commonly observed in foggy or smoky conditions, enhancing beam visibility.

questions.question: What is the product of mass and velocity?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The product of mass and velocity is known as momentum, not impulse. Momentum is a vector quantity that represents the quantity of motion an object has.
 
• Impulse is actually the change in momentum, which is equal to the force applied on an object times the time over which it is applied.
 
• Force is defined as mass times acceleration (Newton's Second Law), not mass times velocity.
 
• Inertia is a property of matter that describes its resistance to any change in its state of motion, including a change in velocity.
 
• Acceleration is a measure of the change in velocity of an object per unit time and is not directly related to the product of mass and velocity.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Impulse
 Impulse is the change in momentum, not the product of mass and velocity.
 
 

 2) Force
 Force is the product of mass and acceleration, according to Newton's Second Law.
 
 

 3) Inertia
 Inertia is a property of matter by which it remains at rest or in uniform motion in the same straight line unless acted upon by some external force.
 
 

 4) Acceleration
 Acceleration is a vector that represents the rate of change of velocity.

• They are not ideal for rear view mirrors in vehicles because they do not cover a wide enough area to be useful for safety purposes.

• **Article 21** of the Constitution of India cannot be amended with a simple majority.
 
• Article 21 guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty, stating that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
